title: Getting started with mcqAnalysis
text: mcqAnalysis package provides unified toolkit classical test theory (CTT) item analysis multiple-choice tests. computes item difficulty, item discrimination (point-biserial correlation upper-lower 27 percent discrimination index), per-distractor analysis, Haladyna’s distractor efficiency, packages results tidy mcq_analysis object dedicated print, plot, apa_table methods. vignette walks complete item analysis using package’s example dataset.

title: Getting started with mcqAnalysis
text: Install released version CRAN: development version GitHub:
code: install.packages("mcqAnalysis") # install.packages("devtools") devtools::install_github("Rafhq1403/mcqAnalysis")

title: Getting started with mcqAnalysis
text: package ships mcq_example, simulated 200-student, 30-item, four-option multiple-choice test. dataset constructed items span full range quality: easy items, ideal medium-difficulty items, hard items declining discrimination, two deliberately badly-written items negative discrimination.
code: data(mcq_example) str(mcq_example, max.level = 1) #> List of 2 #>  $ responses: chr [1:200, 1:30] "D" "D" "D" "D" ... #>   ..- attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2 #>  $ key      : Named chr [1:30] "D" "D" "D" "A" ... #>   ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:30] "item01" "item02" "item03" "item04" ... mcq_example$key[1:6] #> item01 item02 item03 item04 item05 item06  #>    "D"    "D"    "D"    "A"    "D"    "B" head(mcq_example$responses[, 1:6]) #>            item01 item02 item03 item04 item05 item06 #> student001 "D"    "D"    "D"    "A"    "D"    "B"    #> student002 "D"    "D"    "D"    "A"    "A"    "B"    #> student003 "D"    "D"    "C"    "A"    "D"    "B"    #> student004 "D"    "D"    "D"    "A"    "D"    "B"    #> student005 "D"    "D"    "D"    "A"    "D"    "B"    #> student006 "D"    "D"    "D"    "A"    "D"    "B"

title: Getting started with mcqAnalysis
text: wrapper function mcq_analysis() runs every item-level computation single call returns mcq_analysis S3 object. default print method shows test-level summaries (number students, number items, mean SD total scores) item-level table difficulty, point-biserial, discrimination index, distractor efficiency.

title: Getting started with mcqAnalysis
text: plot() method produces difficulty-discrimination scatter — classical “item quality map” used visually identifying items fall outside conventional adequacy cutoffs. default, flagged items labeled, keeping plot legible many items cluster acceptable region.  Items red flagged violate least one default adequacy criteria: difficulty outside [0.30, 0.90] discrimination 0.30. Items 29 30 negative discrimination — high-ability students get wrong often low-ability students, indicating poorly written distractors mis-keyed answer. label every item plot upper-lower 27 percent discrimination index instead point-biserial:
code: plot(result) plot(result, label = "all") plot(result, discrimination_metric = "discrimination_index")

title: Getting started with mcqAnalysis
text: diagnosing specific problematic items, distractor_analysis() function returns per-option breakdown showing response option performed. item-option combination, output reports option’s selection frequency, proportion examinees choosing , whether key, point-biserial correlation total test score. key clearly positive point-biserial; distractor non-trivial selection proportion negative point-biserial. Inspect specific problematic item:
code: da <- distractor_analysis(mcq_example$responses, mcq_example$key) head(da, 8) #>           item option is_key frequency proportion point_biserial #> item01  item01      A  FALSE        10      0.050     -0.2670906 #> item011 item01      B  FALSE        12      0.060     -0.3234223 #> item012 item01      C  FALSE         8      0.040     -0.2505524 #> item013 item01      D   TRUE       170      0.850      0.5156325 #> item02  item02      A  FALSE        10      0.050     -0.2525847 #> item021 item02      B  FALSE         9      0.045     -0.2893215 #> item022 item02      C  FALSE         9      0.045     -0.2550078 #> item023 item02      D   TRUE       172      0.860      0.4838546 da[da$item == "item30", ] #>           item option is_key frequency proportion point_biserial #> item30  item30      A  FALSE        55      0.275     0.27246235 #> item301 item30      B  FALSE        21      0.105     0.04108455 #> item302 item30      C  FALSE        24      0.120    -0.07627404 #> item303 item30      D   TRUE       100      0.500    -0.21893362

title: Getting started with mcqAnalysis
text: distractor_efficiency() summarizes per-option analysis single integer per item: count functioning distractors. distractor “functioning” selected least 5 percent examinees negative point-biserial total score (Haladyna & Downing, 1993). four-option item, distractor efficiency ranges 0 (functioning distractors — item essentially two-option item) 3 (three distractors functioning — item performing full capacity).
code: de <- distractor_efficiency(mcq_example$responses, mcq_example$key) de[1:10] #> item01 item02 item03 item04 item05 item06 item07 item08 item09 item10  #>      2      1      2      2      3      3      3      3      3      3

title: mcqAnalysis
text: mcqAnalysis designed CTT-focused companion sister package contentValidity, computes content-validity indices (-CVI, S-CVI, modified kappa, Aiken’s V, Lawshe’s CVR). Together cover pre-administration content validation (via expert review) post-administration empirical item analysis (via examinee response data) consistent API. inter-rater agreement statistics beyond content validity, see irrCAC; broader psychometric utilities, see psych.

text: Computes Haladyna's distractor efficiency item: number functioning distractors per item. distractor considered functioning meets two criteria: () selected least threshold proportion examinees (default 5 percent), (b) negative point-biserial correlation total test score (Haladyna & Downing, 1993). key (correct answer) excluded count.

title: Item discrimination — item_discrimination

Default 0.27 following Kelley (1939).

title: Item discrimination — item_discrimination
text: named numeric vector discrimination values, one per item.

title: Item discrimination — item_discrimination
text: point-biserial method widely used CTT discrimination index. discrimination index D compares proportion upper-scoring group (top 27 percent total score) answered item correctly proportion lower-scoring group (bottom 27 percent) answered correctly. Kelley (1939) demonstrated 27 percent cutoff maximizes difference extreme groups normal distribution ability. Interpretive guidelines D (Ebel & Frisbie, 1991): D >= 0.40: good item 0.30 <= D < 0.40: good item, possibly subject improvement 0.20 <= D < 0.30: marginal item, needs improvement D < 0.20: poor item, revise discard

title: Item discrimination — item_discrimination
text: Ebel, R. L., & Frisbie, D. . (1991). Essentials educational measurement (5th ed.). Prentice Hall. Kelley, T. L. (1939). selection upper lower groups validation test items. Journal Educational Psychology, 30(1), 17-24.

title: Simulated multiple-choice test data — mcq_example
text: simulated dataset demonstrating mcqAnalysis package. test contains 30 four-option multiple-choice items administered 200 students. data generated two-parameter logistic framework deliberately mixed mix item quality: Items 1-8 easy items strong discrimination. Items 9-24 medium-difficulty items, discriminating well. Items 25-28 harder items progressively weaker discrimination. Items 29-30 deliberately badly-written items negative discrimination (high-ability students get wrong often). Item 30 additionally "trap" distractor disproportionately chosen high-ability students, useful demonstrating distractor analysis.

title: Plot a difficulty-discrimination scatter for an mcq_analysis object — plot.mcq_analysis
text: Produces classical item quality map: scatterplot item difficulty (x-axis) item discrimination (y-axis), reference lines marking conventional adequacy cutoffs. Items upper-middle region (medium difficulty, high discrimination) performing well; items lower regions candidates revision.

title: mcqAnalysis 0.1.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-05-15 Initial CRAN release. Implements classical test theory item analysis multiple-choice tests, including item difficulty (p-value), item discrimination (point-biserial upper-lower 27 percent index), distractor analysis (per-option frequency, proportion, point-biserial), Haladyna’s distractor efficiency. Wrapper function mcq_analysis() returns S3 object print, plot (difficulty-discrimination scatter), apa_table methods. Includes simulated example dataset mcq_example 200 students 30-item four-option test. Verified 78 unit tests using testthat.
